title: Relative flatness and proper annihilator support on algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $M$ a module on the ringed small etale site [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. For every compatible pair of etale scheme charts $U\to X$, $V\to Y$ and $h:U\to V$ over $f$, restrict $M$ to the Zariski scheme module $M_U$ [def-trf-space-module-scheme-restriction]. Define $M$ to be flat over $Y$ if every $M_U$ is flat over $V$ in the affine-local sense [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. For quasi-coherent $M$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] this is equivalently relative geometric-stalk flatness. Define proper annihilator support by the existence of a representable closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ such that $Z\to Y$ is proper [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] and, for every etale scheme chart $T\to X$ and every representing pullback $W\to T$ of $i$, the ideal of $W$ on every affine open $V\subseteq T$ equals $\operatorname{Ann}_{\mathcal O_T(V)}(M_T(V))$. Thus the closed subspace is the annihilator support with its specified ideal structure, not just a proper carrier.
